deck_title: Hooke-Poisson nu=0.5 Hencky lateral contraction vs naive zero-Poisson axial stretch bloat rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Siméon Denis Poisson (1811) & Heinrich Hencky (1928) logarithmic lateral contraction law for incompressible elastomers (Poisson ratio nu = 0.5, transverse logarithmic strain epsilon_perp = -0.5 * ln(lambda_z) so R_perp = R_0 / sqrt(1 + u) and cross-sectional area A_perp = A_0 / (1 + u), locking total volume ratio V/V_0 = 1.0000x across all 17 axial-stretch stations lambda_z = 1 + u in [1.000, 2.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive zero-Poisson axial-only stretching (nu = 0, R_perp = R_0, which bloats cylinder volume by 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-step Hencky logarithmic strain quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Rubber band and slingshot elastic cords, muscular tendon/biceps elongation, stretchy cartoon limbs, and octopus tentacle vertex shaders
Scaling transverse cross-section radius by lambda_z^(-nu) = 1 / sqrt(lambda_z) for nu = 0.5 elastomers so stretched bands naturally neck down and conserve volume
Supporting arbitrary material Poisson ratios nu in [0, 0.5] via Hencky power law R_perp = R_0 * lambda_z^(-nu)
not_for: Honeycomb cork stoppers where Poisson ratio nu is approximately 0.0
Auxetic metamaterials with negative Poisson ratio (nu < 0) that fatten when stretched
